label: input u during original phase, positions 0-5
explanation: Token detector for the letter u as an original input token at positions 0-5. On dev it fires on every such step (precision 1.0) and covers 99.7% of activations. It never fires on u at original positions 6-8, on the delimiter, or on u fed back during copy (only 271 tiny copy-phase activations). Magnitude depends on position and repetition. The strongest activations are at t=2 (top examples are e b u, reaching max 2.147). Activations at t=5 are weak, about 0.2-0.6 of max, and t=5 carries only about 4% of the mass. A repeated u is weaker than the first u in the sequence, about 0.6 of max (in_first=1 holds 93% of mass). Sequence length and digit count have little effect.

issues: Minor: the 245 test misses (271 on dev) are not random. All of them are copy-phase u inputs at t=4 or 5 in L=3 sequences (recall_idx 1-2), each at 0.02-0.13 of max. So the cutoff is really 't <= 5 with input u' rather than 'original phase', but these steps carry 0.0% of the mass. Adding them hurts the score: u & t<=5 & phase!=1 gives test precision 0.968 and F1 0.984, below the original 0.999, because only about 7% of copy-phase u steps at t<=5 fire.

All other claims check out. Precision is 1.0 on both dev and test, with zero false positives. There is no activity at t>=6 or on the delimiter. Mass by t peaks at t=2 (0.244) and t=5 has 0.038. First occurrences carry 93.4% of the mass and repeats 6.6%. Sequence length has little effect: per-L mass is roughly even, apart from fewer eligible steps at short L.
